query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Category (connectivity, email, database) is an intrinsic property of the incident that affects both which technician/handling approach is applied and the resolution time. It is not settable by an actor, so it is a confounder rather than a treatment. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: incident_location_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (network_wide, single_user) reflects intrinsic incident severity/breadth that influences both assignment decisions and resolution time. Immutable given the incident, so a confounder. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: resolution_status
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident is resolved vs open is itself an outcome/status of the resolution process, not a treatment or a common cause. Overlaps with the focus outcome; can act as a selection/collider on resolution_time.

per_column.name: same_technician_assigned_closed
per_column.rationale: Whether the same technician who was assigned also closed the incident is a consequence of the handling process that lies on the path to resolution time; it is downstream of assignment, functioning as a mediator rather than an adjustable confounder.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Who is assigned to an incident is a decision an actor can actually SET or CHANGE, making it a genuine intervenable lever ('assign a different technician to reduce resolution time'). This is a valid what-if treatment.

per_column.name: recurring_incident_pattern
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident is part of a recurring pattern is an intrinsic characteristic that affects both handling/assignment and resolution time. Not settable by an actor; a confounder. Not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The query poses an interventional what-if about reducing resolution_time. One added column, assigned_technician, is a genuinely intervenable treatment (assignment is a decision an actor can set), satisfying part (a). Several columns (incident_category, incident_location_scope, recurring_incident_pattern) are plausible confounders that are common causes of both assignment and resolution time and were NOT named in the query, demonstrating the capability under test. However, the set is imperfect: same_technician_assigned_closed is a mediator, and resolution_status is an outcome/collider rather than a confounder, and the confounders are intrinsic incident attributes of moderate strength. Overall the intervention structure is partially realised.
